title: The Safeguard Comes Before the Cut

scenes.tts: How can a cell be ready to destroy itself within hours, and still never do it by mistake? The killer is an enzyme called a caspase. It cuts other proteins. Nothing undoes a cut. So where can the cell place its safeguard?
scenes.visual: A clock sweeps beside a red caspase chip; a crossed-out mistake chip. The caspase cuts a grey protein bar in two; the halves try to rejoin and the way back is struck out. A dashed box with a question mark appears in front of the caspase.
scenes.narration: How can a cell be ready to destroy itself within hours, and still never do it by mistake? The killer is an enzyme called a caspase. It cuts other proteins. Nothing undoes a cut. So where can the cell place its safeguard?

scenes.tts: Every caspase is made ahead of time, as an inactive precursor, so it is ready to act. An initiator, such as caspase nine, starts as a single inactive chain. It turns on only when a platform gathers several copies, and they pair up. Then it cuts an executioner caspase, which is already paired but inactive. So the first step is a gathering, and every step after it is a cut.
scenes.caption: Every caspase is made ahead of time, as an inactive precursor, so it is ready to act. An initiator, such as caspase-9, starts as a single inactive chain. It turns on only when a platform gathers several copies, and they pair up. Then it cuts an executioner caspase, which is already paired but inactive. So the first step is a gathering, and every step after it is a cut.
scenes.visual: Four dashed caspase chains drift loose. A teal platform bar appears; the chains gather on it and pair up, turning solid red. The active pair cuts a dashed paired executioner, which turns solid. Labels mark the platform as the gathering and the executioner's cut as the cut.
scenes.narration: Every caspase is made ahead of time, as an inactive precursor, so it is ready to act. An initiator, such as caspase-9, starts as a single inactive chain. It turns on only when a platform gathers several copies, and they pair up. Then it cuts an executioner caspase, which is already paired but inactive. So the first step is a gathering, and every step after it is a cut.

scenes.tts: One part of the platform, Apaf one, sits in the cytosol. The other part, cytochrome c, is kept behind the outer membrane of the mitochondrion, so no platform forms. If that membrane opens, cytochrome c escapes. Cytochrome c and the nucleotide D A T P then make seven copies of Apaf one assemble into a wheel. This wheel, the apoptosome, gathers caspase nine.
scenes.caption: One part of the platform, APAF-1, sits in the cytosol. The other part, cytochrome c, is kept behind the outer membrane of the mitochondrion, so no platform forms. If that membrane opens, cytochrome c escapes. Cytochrome c and the nucleotide dATP then make seven copies of APAF-1 assemble into a wheel. This wheel, the apoptosome, gathers caspase-9.
scenes.visual: Cytosol on top, the mitochondrion below behind a grey membrane bar. Teal APAF-1 blobs are scattered above, orange cytochrome c discs sit below the membrane, and a dashed ghost wheel is struck out. A pore opens in the membrane, the discs rise through it, and seven teal blobs close into a wheel with a disc on each; dashed red caspase chains fly to its hub.
scenes.narration: One part of the platform, APAF-1, sits in the cytosol. The other part, cytochrome c, is kept behind the outer membrane of the mitochondrion, so no platform forms. If that membrane opens, cytochrome c escapes. Cytochrome c and the nucleotide dATP then make seven copies of APAF-1 assemble into a wheel. This wheel, the apoptosome, gathers caspase-9.

scenes.tts: At that membrane, a family of proteins named for B C L two decides, and it has three classes. Bax and Bak, the effectors, open the outer membrane once they are activated. B C L two and its relatives, the guards, hold them in check. The sensors, such as Bad and Bid, carry a short helix that fills a guard's groove. Some also switch on Bax.
scenes.caption: At that membrane, a family of proteins named for BCL-2 decides, and it has three classes. BAX and BAK, the effectors, open the outer membrane once they are activated. BCL-2 and its relatives, the guards, hold them in check. The sensors, such as BAD and BID, carry a short helix that fills a guard's groove. Some also switch on BAX.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the outer membrane: purple BAX and BAK sit either side of a closed stretch, each with a green guard beside it and a green hold bar between them. Yellow sensors with a small helix capsule drop in from above; one capsule slides into the groove on a guard and fills it.
scenes.narration: At that membrane, a family of proteins named for BCL-2 decides, and it has three classes. BAX and BAK, the effectors, open the outer membrane once they are activated. BCL-2 and its relatives, the guards, hold them in check. The sensors, such as BAD and BID, carry a short helix that fills a guard's groove. Some also switch on BAX.

scenes.tts: In a healthy cell, guards and effectors are both present. Their amounts and binding set how hard the cell must be pushed. A stress must switch on enough sensors to tie up the guards. Then the guards are occupied, Bax and Bak are free, and the membrane opens. Cytochrome c escapes from the mitochondrion.
scenes.caption: In a healthy cell, guards and effectors are both present. Their amounts and binding set how hard the cell must be pushed. A stress must switch on enough sensors to tie up the guards. Then the guards are occupied, BAX and BAK are free, and the membrane opens. Cytochrome c escapes from the mitochondrion.
scenes.visual: A balance on top: green guards in the left pan outweigh one yellow sensor in the right pan, and the membrane strip below is shut with BAX and BAK held. Sensors are added until they outnumber the guards and the beam tips. Helices fill every guard groove, the hold bars drop away, the membrane opens and orange cytochrome c rises through the gap.
scenes.narration: In a healthy cell, guards and effectors are both present. Their amounts and binding set how hard the cell must be pushed. A stress must switch on enough sensors to tie up the guards. Then the guards are occupied, BAX and BAK are free, and the membrane opens. Cytochrome c escapes from the mitochondrion.

scenes.tts: Now follow the whole chain, in order. Enough sensors tie up the guards, and Bax and Bak open the membrane. Cytochrome c escapes, and the wheel assembles and gathers caspase nine. Then the cuts begin, one after another. Keep this rule: the balance of guards and sensors mostly decides before the first cut, since no cut is undone.

scenes.visual: Five small pictures in a row, each lighting up as it is named: a tipped balance, a membrane with a gap, orange discs rising, the teal wheel, a red cut. Arrows join them. A bracket marks the balance as the decision; the last step has an undo arrow struck out.
